chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abu al-Abbas al-Baqbaq and 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would increase in his prayer during the month of Ramadan. When he prayed the 'Isha prayer, he would pray after it. The people would stand behind him, so he would enter and leave them, then he would come out again, and they would come and stand behind him, so he would enter and leave them, repeatedly.
He said, and he said: 'Do not pray after the 'Isha prayer in months other than Ramadan.'
ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet's specific method of praying extra night prayers during Ramadan according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) unique practice of performing extra night prayers after 'Isha specifically in Ramadan, characterized by a distinctive ritual of repeatedly entering and exiting the prayer space while the congregation waited. Scholars interpret this 'repeated entry and exit' as either a sign of humility, a method to encourage the companions to follow, or a specific Sunnah of *Tarawih* that distinguishes Ramadan from other months, as the Prophet explicitly restricted this particular mode of worship to the holy month alone.
